title: Derivatives
description: Options, futures, and structured products — the building blocks of payoff engineering. Curated for members who want to go from comfortable with linear instruments to comfortable with convexity.

resources.title: Tim Bennett — Derivatives
resources.note: A short and very well done course on derivatives. Tim Bennett is a great speaker in general.

resources.title: projectoption
resources.note: Options trading and explanations.

title: Finance theory
description: Academic foundations of modern finance — pricing theory, portfolio construction, and how markets actually clear. Useful before tackling a quant pitch or sitting in on a Quant Department session.

resources.title: MIT 15.401 — Finance Theory I (Andrew Lo)
resources.note: MIT's introductory finance course taught by Andrew Lo. Time value of money, CAPM, portfolio theory, market efficiency — the core theoretical framework every analyst should be able to derive from first principles.

resources.title: Portfolio Theory (MIT 18.S096)
resources.note: Mean-variance optimisation, factor models, risk parity, and the math behind portfolio construction. The applied complement to Markowitz's original paper.

resources.title: Financial Markets Microstructure — Egor Starkov (UCPH)
resources.note: How prices actually form: order books, market makers, information asymmetry, liquidity, market design. Essential before any quant or execution-focused work.

resources.title: MIT 18.S096 — Topics in Mathematics with Applications in Finance
resources.note: MIT's quantitative finance course. PCA, regression, time series, stochastic processes — the bridge between the pure-math playlists and applied quant work.

title: Geopolitics & macro
description: Channels and primers that build a working macro and geopolitics frame — the backdrop every pitch sits inside. Useful before writing the macro section of a pitch or sitting in on a Macro Department session.

resources.title: Patrick Boyle
resources.note: Geopolitics and macro coverage. Also has good older videos on financial markets theory.

resources.title: Principles for Dealing with the Changing World Order — Ray Dalio
resources.note: Dalio's framework for the Big Cycle of empires — debt, money, internal conflict, external conflict — applied across 500 years of history. The macro lens behind almost every Bridgewater note.

resources.title: Principles for Navigating Big Debt Crises — Ray Dalio
resources.note: A full template for how debt cycles unfold, with 48 case studies including 1929, Weimar, and 2008. The book to read before any sovereign-credit or macro-rates pitch.

resources.title: How the Economic Machine Works — Ray Dalio
resources.note: Dalio's 30-minute animated explainer of the credit-driven business cycle. The single best primer on macroeconomics for a finance student.

title: Hedge funds & legendary investors
description: Biographies, interviews, and case histories of the people who actually made the returns. Useful for seeing how the strategies in the textbooks look when run by a fund manager facing the market.

resources.title: The Man Who Solved the Market — Gregory Zuckerman
resources.note: How Jim Simons and Renaissance Technologies built the most successful quant fund in history — the Medallion Fund's average annual return is 66% since 1988. Essential context for anyone curious about systematic strategies.

resources.title: Intelligent Investing with Steve Forbes
resources.note: Long-form interviews with the best minds in active management — Bogle, Greenblatt, Novogratz, Whitney, and more. The conversation versions of the books elsewhere in this directory.

title: Investing classics
description: The core canon of value, growth, and common-sense investing — books that turn up on every PMC senior analyst's shelf. Read these before the first pitch you sit on.

resources.title: Principles — Ray Dalio
resources.note: Bridgewater's founder lays out his operating principles for life, work, and managing teams under uncertainty. Required reading for anyone running a process under pressure.

resources.title: The Psychology of Money — Morgan Housel
resources.note: Nineteen short essays on why money decisions get made at the dinner table, not on a spreadsheet. The behavioural finance text written by someone who can actually write.

resources.title: The Little Book That Beats the Market — Joel Greenblatt
resources.note: The Magic Formula explained in plain English: buy good businesses at low prices, systematically, and let the math run. The cleanest one-sitting introduction to quantitative value.

resources.title: The Big Secret for the Small Investor — Joel Greenblatt
resources.note: Greenblatt's follow-up: why small investors have a structural edge over institutional money, and how to actually use it. Less famous than the Magic Formula book; arguably more important.

resources.title: The Little Book of Common Sense Investing — John C. Bogle
resources.note: Vanguard's founder makes the case that the most reliable path to long-term return is to own the market at the lowest possible cost. The argument every active manager has to be able to answer.

resources.title: One Up on Wall Street — Peter Lynch
resources.note: Magellan-era Lynch on how retail investors can outperform pros by paying attention to what they already buy. The original 'invest in what you know' playbook.

title: Mathematical foundations
description: The math behind quant finance — linear algebra, calculus, differential equations, stochastic calculus, game theory, econometrics. The toolkit Quant Department members assume you have on day one.

resources.title: MIT 18.06 — Linear Algebra (Gilbert Strang)
resources.note: The reference course for linear algebra, taught by Gilbert Strang himself. Vectors, matrices, eigenvalues, SVD — the operations that underpin every factor model and quant trade.

resources.title: 3Blue1Brown — Essence of Linear Algebra
resources.note: Grant Sanderson's visual companion to Strang. Watch this if matrices feel symbolic and abstract — the geometric intuition makes the same content feel mechanical.

resources.title: MIT 18.01 — Single Variable Calculus
resources.note: Derivatives and integrals from first principles. The math foundation everything in continuous-time finance is built on top of.

resources.title: Multivariable Calculus
resources.note: Partial derivatives, gradients, Lagrange multipliers — required for portfolio optimisation, risk decomposition, and most of the dual variables in pricing.

resources.title: 3Blue1Brown — Differential Equations
resources.note: Visual intro to ODEs and dynamical systems. The right place to start if you've never solved a differential equation outside of a calculator.

resources.title: MIT 18.03 — Differential Equations
resources.note: Alessandro's pick as the best playlist for differential equations. The full rigorous treatment, including the systems-of-equations cases that show up in macro modelling.

resources.title: Differential Equations — additional course
resources.note: A supplementary playlist for working through more ODE examples once the MIT and 3Blue1Brown material clicks.

resources.title: Stochastic Calculus for Finance
resources.note: Brownian motion, Itô's lemma, the Black-Scholes derivation — the machinery behind derivatives pricing. The math jump from ODEs to SDEs is the single biggest step in quant finance.

resources.title: Stochastic Calculus — visually explained
resources.note: Visual companion to the stochastic calculus playlist. Helpful if Itô's lemma still feels symbolic the first time through.

resources.title: Game Theory 101 — William Spaniel
resources.note: Nash equilibrium, subgame-perfect, Bayesian — the full canonical course in plain English. Useful far beyond auction theory: every negotiation, every information game, every signalling story in finance.

resources.title: Ben Lambert (SpartacanUsuals) — Econometrics
resources.note: Ben Lambert's playlists span undergraduate to PhD-level econometrics — OLS, GMM, time series, Bayesian methods. Pick the playlist that matches the level you need.

title: Private equity
description: From fund mechanics and LBO basics through evergreen vehicles and the secondaries market. Useful before sitting in on a Private Equity learning session or working on a pitch involving buyout-backed names.

resources.title: Claudia Zeisberger
resources.note: Private equity coverage from the basics through advanced topics like evergreen funds and the secondaries market. INSEAD professor; concise, structured, and accurate on fund mechanics.

title: Probabilistic thinking
description: Books on luck, uncertainty, reflexivity, and asymmetric payoffs — the mental models that separate analysts who got lucky from analysts who understand they got lucky.

resources.title: The Alchemy of Finance — George Soros
resources.note: Soros lays out his theory of reflexivity: market participants' perceptions don't just observe prices, they create them. The book behind every macro hedge fund's risk frame.

resources.title: Fooled by Randomness — Nassim Nicholas Taleb
resources.note: Alessandro's absolute-must-read of the four Taleb books. How traders mistake luck for skill, and the survivorship bias that makes the mistake invisible until it isn't.

resources.title: The Black Swan — Nassim Nicholas Taleb
resources.note: Highly improbable events that, in hindsight, look obvious. The book that put fat-tailed thinking into the financial mainstream — and explains why most risk models break exactly when they need to work.

resources.title: Skin in the Game — Nassim Nicholas Taleb
resources.note: Why agents without downside exposure to their own decisions distort every system they touch — finance, medicine, journalism. The asymmetry framework behind every alignment-of-interest argument.

resources.title: Antifragile — Nassim Nicholas Taleb
resources.note: The complement to Black Swan: how to build positions, portfolios, and lives that gain from volatility rather than break under it. The constructive finish to the Incerto series.

title: Valuation
description: How to value a business — DCFs, multiples, intrinsic value, and the edge cases that break textbook frameworks. Required before owning the financial-model slide in any pitch.

resources.title: Aswath Damodaran — Valuation (NYU Stern)
resources.note: Damodaran's full NYU MBA Valuation course on YouTube, free. The reference course for DCF, multiples, real options, and the corner cases textbooks gloss over. Watch the parts that match your pitch.
